parts.text: A student is determining the spring constant k of a spring. Fig. 1.1 shows the apparatus used. Fig. 1.1

parts.label: a
parts.text: (a) On Fig. 1.1, measure the unstretched length l 0 of the coiled part of the spring, in mm. Record this value of length l in Table 1.1 for L = 0.00 N. [1]

parts.label: b
parts.text: (b) On Fig. 1.1, show how a set-square could be used to take readings in order to determine the length l 0 of the coiled part of the spring. [1]

ms.label: 1(b)
ms.text: recognisable set-square shown from spring to rule along one of the dotted lines

parts.label: c
parts.text: (c) The student places a 0.20 N load on the spring. He records the new length l of the spring in Table 1.1. He repeats the procedure using loads of 0.40 N, 0.60 N, 0.80 N and 1.00 N. All the readings are recorded in Table 1.1.

parts.label: i
parts.text: (i) Calculate the extension e of the spring for each value of load L , using the equation e = ( l – l 0 ). Record the values of e in Table 1.1. [1]

parts.label: ii
parts.text: (ii) Complete the column headings in Table 1.1. Table 1.1 L / l / e / 0.00 0 0.20 31 0.40 40 0.60 46 0.80 55 1.00 63 [1]

parts.label: d
parts.text: (d) Plot a graph of L / N ( y -axis) against e / mm ( x -axis). [4]

ms.label: 1(d)
ms.text:
Graph:
axes correctly labelled and right way round
suitable scales, at least ½ the grid used
all plots correct to ½ small square
good line judgement, thin, continuous line

parts.label: e
parts.text: (e) Determine the gradient G of the graph. Show clearly on the graph how you obtained the necessary information. G = .......................................................... [2]

ms.label: 1(e)
ms.text:
triangle method used and seen on graph
at least half of candidate’s line used

parts.label: f
parts.text: (f) The gradient G is numerically equal to the spring constant k . Write down a value for k to a suitable number of significant figures for this experiment. k = .............................................. N / mm [1]

ms.label: 1(f)
ms.text: answers within the range 0.025 ± 0.005 (N / mm) and expressed to 2 / 3 significant figures only
